title: What the grammar forbids

data.source: Four made-up event records of 400 gaps each, two toy counters and five toy memories, all generated in the script (seed 20261118). Adapted from colloquy/lab/philosophical/grammar_forbids.py.

prediction: Carrier free, nothing is refused; typed, the leaky counter and the trend-follower are refused.
baseline: A plain threshold-and-reset description under the same typing (no memory rule), and the decoy rule "accept every record".
why: With the carrier left free, R1 to R3 wrote down every record we tried, so they forbid nothing. With the carrier and constants declared first (a museum variant), the same lines refused a leaky counter, a trend-follower and an AR(2) memory. Four of the lens's five written predictions held; E2 missed for the speeding-up record.
claim_kind: philosophical correspondence (the content of the grammar itself); not a claim about the world
variant: V-philosophical-1 (the typed grammar): a museum experiment, not the owner's CRR

forks.what: twenty other seeds for the made-up records

second_check: adapted and re-run by a library worker who did not write the mapping; not checked by a person
variants: V-philosophical-1 (the typed grammar): a museum experiment, not the owner's CRR
operating_characteristics: Deterministic arithmetic on declared records: the rule prints the same verdict every time, so the outcome weighs only on what the grammar says, not on the world.
